board_events.text: After the first polaroid the intensity is $I_0/2$. The middle polaroid is at $\phi$ to the first; the last is at $90^\circ$ to the first, hence at $\left(90^\circ - \phi\right)$ to the middle one.
Now simplify with the double-angle identity $\cos\phi\,\sin\phi = \tfrac{1}{2}\sin 2\phi$.
Interpretation: the middle polaroid should BISECT the angle between the crossed pair. Each Malus factor is then $\cos^{2}45^\circ = \tfrac{1}{2}$.
A system that passed nothing now passes one eighth of the input. That is the elegant sting of this problem.

segments.text: The Advanced version of the same setup, and instead of a single number it asks for a function and then an optimisation. The physics is identical; the extra demand is algebraic care.

Two polaroids are crossed. A third is inserted between them with its pass axis at angle phi to the first. For unpolarised input of intensity I nought, find the transmitted intensity as a function of phi, and then find the phi that maximises it.
The figure shows where we are heading. Transmitted intensity plotted against the middle polaroid's angle, rising from zero, peaking, and falling back to zero.

Step one, build the expression. After the first polaroid the intensity is I nought over two. The middle polaroid is at phi to the first, and the last is at ninety degrees to the first, which puts it at ninety degrees minus phi relative to the middle one.

Applying Malus twice gives I of phi equals I nought over two, times cosine squared phi, times cosine squared of ninety minus phi. And cosine of ninety minus phi is sine phi, so that second factor is sine squared phi.
Step two, simplify. The product cosine phi sine phi is one half sine two phi, by the double-angle identity. Squaring that gives one quarter sine squared two phi.

So I of phi equals I nought over two, times one quarter, times sine squared two phi, which is I nought over eight, times sine squared two phi. That is the function asked for, and it is much easier to maximise in this form.
Step three, maximise. Sine squared of two phi is maximum, equal to one, when two phi equals ninety degrees, so phi equals forty five degrees, and the maximum intensity is I nought over eight.

Interpret it physically, because Advanced papers reward that. The middle polaroid should bisect the angle between the crossed pair. When it does, each Malus factor is cosine squared forty five, which is one half, so the chain reads a half, times a half, times a half.

And step back to see what has happened. A system that passed absolutely nothing now passes one eighth of the input, purely because you inserted another absorber and aimed it correctly. That is the elegant sting of this problem.
उसी setup का Advanced रूप, और यहाँ एक अकेले number की जगह पहले एक function माँगा जाता है, फिर उसका optimisation। Physics वही है; अतिरिक्त माँग algebra की सावधानी है।

दो polaroids crossed हैं। बीच में एक तीसरा डाला गया है जिसका pass axis पहले से phi angle पर है। I nought intensity की unpolarised input के लिए transmitted intensity phi के function के रूप में निकालिए, और फिर वो phi जो उसे maximum करे।
Figure बता रही है हम कहाँ पहुँचने वाले हैं। बीच वाले polaroid के angle के मुक़ाबले transmitted intensity, zero से उठती, चोटी बनाती, और वापस zero पर गिरती।

पहला step, expression बनाइए। पहले polaroid के बाद intensity I nought बटा दो है। बीच वाला polaroid पहले से phi पर है, और आख़िरी पहले से नब्बे degree पर, जो उसे बीच वाले के मुक़ाबले नब्बे degree minus phi पर रख देता है।

Malus दो बार लगाने पर I of phi बराबर I nought बटा दो, गुणा cosine squared phi, गुणा cosine squared of नब्बे minus phi। और cosine of नब्बे minus phi तो sine phi है, तो दूसरा factor sine squared phi बन जाता है।
दूसरा step, simplify कीजिए। गुणनफल cosine phi sine phi, double-angle identity से, आधा sine दो phi है। उसका square लीजिए तो एक चौथाई sine squared दो phi।
तो I of phi बराबर I nought बटा दो, गुणा एक चौथाई, गुणा sine squared दो phi, यानी I nought बटा आठ, गुणा sine squared दो phi। यही माँगा गया function है, और इस रूप में इसे maximise करना कहीं आसान है।
तीसरा step, maximise कीजिए। sine squared of दो phi तब maximum यानी एक होता है जब दो phi बराबर नब्बे degree हो, यानी phi बराबर पैंतालीस degree, और maximum intensity है I nought बटा आठ।

इसे physically समझाइए, क्योंकि Advanced के papers उसका इनाम देते हैं। बीच वाले polaroid को crossed जोड़ी के angle को आधा-आधा बाँटना चाहिए। ऐसा होने पर हर Malus factor cosine squared पैंतालीस यानी आधा हो जाता है, तो पूरी chain बनती है आधा, गुणा आधा, गुणा आधा।

और एक क़दम पीछे हटकर देखिए क्या हुआ। जो system बिल्कुल कुछ नहीं भेजता था, वो अब input का आठवाँ हिस्सा भेज रहा है, सिर्फ़ इसलिए कि आपने एक और सोखने वाली चीज़ डाली और उसे सही दिशा में ताना। यही इस सवाल का ख़ूबसूरत डंक है।

sections.title: Four polarisation pitfalls and the half-then-chain routine

board_events.text: Polarisation pitfalls and the half-then-chain routine
1. Skipping the $I_0/2$ at the first polaroid. Unpolarised light entering the first polaroid is ALWAYS halved, whatever its orientation.
2. Applying Malus's law to unpolarised light. $I_0\cos^{2}\theta$ needs a defined incident polarisation - use it only from the second polaroid onward.
3. Measuring Malus angles from the wrong reference. Each angle is measured between CONSECUTIVE polaroids, not from the first one. Track the running orientation.
4. Forgetting that Brewster's angle is an angle of INCIDENCE. $\tan i_B = n$ gives the incidence angle; the refraction angle is its complement, $90^\circ - i_B$.
The routine: write $I_0/2$ for the first polaroid, then multiply by $\cos^{2}(\Delta\theta)$ for each subsequent one, where $\Delta\theta$ is the angle to the PREVIOUS polaroid.
Sanity checks: crossed polaroids give zero; inserting one between them always lets some light back through; and the most a two-polaroid stack can pass from unpolarised input is $I_0/2$.
Half first, cosine-squared the rest. And transverse polarises, longitudinal cannot.

segments.text: Four pitfalls and one routine close this subtopic, and with it the teaching content of the chapter.

Pitfall one, skipping the half at the first polaroid. Unpolarised light entering the first polaroid is always halved, whatever its orientation. Forgetting this throws off every multi-polaroid numerical by a factor of two, and the error propagates silently through the rest of the chain.

Pitfall two, applying Malus's law to unpolarised light. I nought cosine squared theta needs a defined incident polarisation direction. Use it only for light that is already polarised, which in practice means from the second polaroid onward.

Pitfall three, measuring Malus angles from the wrong reference. In a stack, each angle is measured between consecutive polaroids, not from the first one. We saw exactly this in the three-polaroid problem, where the third was at sixty degrees to the second, not thirty.

Pitfall four, forgetting that Brewster's angle is an angle of incidence. Tangent i B equals n gives you the incidence angle. The refraction angle is its complement, ninety degrees minus i B. Questions that hand you the refraction angle are testing precisely this.
Now the routine, and almost every polaroid problem you will ever be set is this one line.

Write I nought over two for the first polaroid, then multiply by cosine squared of delta theta for each subsequent polaroid, where delta theta is the angle to the previous one. That is it. A chain of cosine squares hanging off a single half.

Keep three sanity checks running alongside. Crossed polaroids give zero. Inserting one in between always lets some light back through. And the most a two-polaroid stack can ever pass, from unpolarised input, is I nought over two.
Two sentences to carry into the exam. Half first, cosine-squared the rest. And transverse polarises, longitudinal cannot.
चार pitfalls और एक routine के साथ ये subtopic ख़त्म, और इसी के साथ chapter का teaching content भी।

पहला pitfall, पहले polaroid पर आधा छोड़ देना। पहले polaroid में घुसती unpolarised light हमेशा आधी होती है, चाहे वो किसी भी तरफ़ घुमा हो। इसे भूलना हर multi-polaroid numerical को दो के factor से बिगाड़ देता है, और वो ग़लती बाक़ी पूरी chain में चुपचाप आगे बढ़ती जाती है।

दूसरा pitfall, unpolarised light पर Malus's law लगाना। I nought cosine squared theta को एक तय incident polarisation दिशा चाहिए। इसे सिर्फ़ उस light पर लगाइए जो पहले से polarised है, यानी practically दूसरे polaroid से आगे।

तीसरा pitfall, Malus के angles ग़लत reference से नापना। ढेर में हर angle लगातार दो polaroids के बीच नापा जाता है, पहले वाले से नहीं। तीन polaroid वाले सवाल में हमने यही देखा, जहाँ तीसरा दूसरे से साठ degree पर था, तीस नहीं।

चौथा pitfall, ये भूल जाना कि Brewster का angle एक angle of incidence है। tangent i B बराबर n आपको incidence वाला angle देता है। Refraction वाला angle उसका पूरक है, नब्बे degree minus i B। जो सवाल आपको refraction angle थमा दे, वो ठीक यही जाँच रहा है।
अब routine, और आपको मिलने वाला लगभग हर polaroid सवाल इसी एक line में है।

पहले polaroid के लिए I nought बटा दो लिखिए, फिर हर अगले polaroid के लिए cosine squared of delta theta से गुणा कीजिए, जहाँ delta theta पिछले polaroid से बना angle है। बस इतना ही। एक अकेले आधे से लटकती cosine squares की एक chain।

साथ में तीन sanity checks चलाते रहिए। Crossed polaroids zero देते हैं। बीच में एक डालने पर हमेशा कुछ light वापस निकलने लगती है। और unpolarised input से दो polaroid का ढेर ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा I nought बटा दो ही भेज सकता है।
Exam में ले जाने के लिए दो वाक्य। पहले आधा, बाक़ी सब cosine squared। और transverse polarise होती है, longitudinal नहीं हो सकती।

sections.title: Complete formula recap for Wave Optics

board_events.text: Your complete Wave Optics toolkit

board_events.latex: 2nt\cos r = \left(m+\tfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda \;\text{(reflected bright)}, \quad = m\lambda \;\text{(reflected dark)}, \qquad t_{\min} = \frac{\lambda}{4n_{\text{coat}}}, \qquad \rho_m = \sqrt{m\lambda R}
I = \frac{I_0}{2} \;\text{(unpolarised through one)}, \qquad I = I_0\cos^{2}\theta, \qquad \tan i_B = n, \qquad i_B + r = 90^\circ

board_events.text: Every line on this board follows from one idea: light is a wave, and Huygens' construction tells it where to go next.

segments.text: Here is your complete toolkit for Wave Optics, on one board. This is not a re-teach. It is the consolidated list, in the order the chapter built it, for the night before the exam.

First line, from wavefronts and Huygens. Refractive index as c over v, the full Snell chain linking sines, speeds, indices and wavelengths, the medium wavelength as lambda over n, and the one thing that never changes, frequency.

Second line, the two scaling laws. Intensity falling as one over r squared while amplitude falls only as one over r, and the Fresnel distance a squared over lambda, marking where ray optics hands over to wave optics.
Third line, Doppler. The frequency form with its minus sign, the wavelength form with its plus, the speed extracted from a measured shift, and the exact relativistic formula for completeness.

Fourth line, the double slit. Path difference as d sine theta, or y d over D near the axis, the bridge from path to phase, and the two conditions: whole wavelengths for bright, odd half wavelengths for dark.

Fifth line, everything else from the double slit. Fringe width lambda D over d, angular fringe width lambda over d, fringe width in a medium, the cosine-squared intensity with its half angle, and the contrast ratio in terms of amplitudes.

Sixth line, thin films. Two n t cosine r as the reflected bright condition with the extra half, the same expression equal to m lambda for reflected dark, the quarter-wave anti-reflection thickness, and the Newton's dark ring radius.

Seventh line, diffraction. A sine theta equals m lambda, and note the capital letters on the board: that is minima, not maxima. Then the angular and linear widths of the central maximum, and the two resolution limits, Rayleigh for a telescope and the numerical-aperture form for a microscope.
Eighth line, polarisation. The half rule for unpolarised light through one polaroid, Malus's law for everything after that, Brewster's law, and the perpendicularity condition that produces it.
And the sentence under all of it. Every line on this board follows from one idea. Light is a wave, and Huygens' construction tells it where to go next.
ये रहा आपका पूरा Wave Optics toolkit, एक ही board पर। ये दोबारा पढ़ाना नहीं है। ये समेटी हुई सूची है, उसी क्रम में जिसमें chapter ने इसे बनाया, exam से एक रात पहले के लिए।

पहली line, wavefronts और Huygens से। Refractive index c बटा v, पूरी Snell chain जो sines, speeds, indices और wavelengths को जोड़ती है, medium की wavelength lambda बटा n, और वो एक चीज़ जो कभी नहीं बदलती, frequency।

दूसरी line, दो scaling laws। Intensity one बटा r squared की तरह गिरती है जबकि amplitude सिर्फ़ one बटा r की तरह, और Fresnel distance a squared बटा lambda, जो बताता है ray optics कहाँ wave optics को सौंप देती है।
तीसरी line, Doppler। Frequency वाला रूप अपने minus के साथ, wavelength वाला अपने plus के साथ, नापे गए shift से निकाली गई speed, और पूरा करने के लिए exact relativistic formula।
चौथी line, double slit। Path difference d sine theta, या axis के पास y d बटा D, path से phase तक का पुल, और दोनों conditions: bright के लिए पूरी wavelengths, dark के लिए आधी wavelengths के विषम गुणज।

पाँचवीं line, double slit से बाक़ी सब कुछ। Fringe width lambda D बटा d, angular fringe width lambda बटा d, medium में fringe width, half angle वाली cosine-squared intensity, और amplitudes में contrast ratio।

छठी line, thin films। दो n t cosine r, reflected bright condition उस अतिरिक्त आधे के साथ, वही expression reflected dark के लिए m lambda के बराबर, quarter-wave anti-reflection मोटाई, और Newton की dark ring की radius।

सातवीं line, diffraction। a sine theta बराबर m lambda, और board पर बड़े अक्षर देखिए: ये minima हैं, maxima नहीं। फिर central maximum की angular और linear widths, और दोनों resolution limits, telescope के लिए Rayleigh और microscope के लिए numerical-aperture वाला रूप।
आठवीं line, polarisation। एक polaroid से गुज़रती unpolarised light के लिए आधे वाला नियम, उसके बाद हर चीज़ के लिए Malus's law, Brewster's law, और वो perpendicularity की शर्त जो उसे पैदा करती है।
और इन सबके नीचे वो एक वाक्य। इस board की हर line एक ही idea से निकलती है। Light एक wave है, और Huygens की construction उसे बताती है कि आगे कहाँ जाना है।

board_events.text: WAVEFRONT: locus of points in the same phase; ray is perpendicular to it. Point source gives spherical, line source cylindrical, far source plane. Huygens: every point is a secondary source, and the envelope of the wavelets is the new wavefront. Conserved on refraction: frequency. Changed: speed and wavelength.

DOPPLER: receding gives redshift, longer wavelength and lower frequency; approaching gives blueshift. Only the radial component counts. Factor of 2 when the wave reflects off a mover, or when two opposite edges are compared.

INTERFERENCE: coherent sources mean a constant phase difference - two independent bulbs give NO fringes. Central fringe always bright. Fringe width is uniform and independent of the order. A denser medium shrinks it. A glass sheet over one slit shifts the pattern without changing the spacing.

THIN FILM: division of amplitude. Half-wave loss at every rarer-into-denser reflection. Reflected and transmitted conditions are complementary. A very thin film looks black in reflection. Anti-reflection coating is a quarter-wave layer. Newton's rings have a dark centre, and shrink by root n in a liquid.

DIFFRACTION: bending at apertures, visible when the aperture is comparable to the wavelength. It is one wavefront interfering with itself. The minima condition is the opposite of the double-slit bright condition. The central maximum is twice as wide and by far the brightest. Bigger aperture means finer resolution.

POLARISATION: only transverse waves polarise, so light is transverse and sound cannot be polarised. Halve at the first polaroid, then cosine squared for each one after. Crossed polaroids pass nothing. Brewster: the reflected ray is perpendicular to the refracted ray.
Mnemonics: 'big n, slow and short' - 'red is receding' - 'order m, index n' - 'two-en-tee, mind the half' - 'd for double and bright, a for aperture and dark' - 'half first, cosine-squared the rest'.
That is Wave Optics end to end. Every formula you have met is a consequence of treating light as a wave and asking, at each surface or aperture, where the wavefront goes next.

segments.text: Final section of the chapter: the quick-recall sheet. Read this the morning of the exam, and nothing else.

Start with the map. One idea at the top, wavefronts and Huygens' principle, and four consequences hanging off it: Doppler, interference, diffraction, polarisation. Everything you have learned sits somewhere on this diagram.

Wavefront and Huygens. Locus of points in the same phase, with the ray perpendicular to it. Point source spherical, line source cylindrical, far source plane. Every point becomes a secondary source and the envelope of the wavelets is the new front. Frequency is conserved on refraction; speed and wavelength are not.

Doppler. Receding gives redshift, meaning longer wavelength and lower frequency. Approaching gives blueshift. Only the radial component counts, and look for a factor of two whenever the wave bounces off a mover or two opposite edges are compared.

Interference. Coherent means a constant phase difference, so two independent bulbs give no fringes at all. The central fringe is always bright. Fringe width is uniform and independent of the order. A denser medium shrinks it, and a glass sheet over one slit shifts the pattern without changing the spacing.

Thin film. Division of amplitude, with a half-wave loss at every rarer-into-denser reflection. Reflected and transmitted conditions are complementary. A very thin film looks black in reflection. An anti-reflection coating is a quarter-wave layer, and Newton's rings have a dark centre and shrink by root n in a liquid.

Diffraction. Bending at apertures, visible when the aperture is comparable to the wavelength, and it is really one wavefront interfering with itself. The minima condition looks identical to the double-slit bright condition and means the opposite. The central maximum is twice as wide and far the brightest. Bigger aperture means finer resolution.

Polarisation. Only transverse waves polarise, which is why light can be polarised and sound cannot. Halve at the first polaroid, then a cosine squared for each one after that. Crossed polaroids pass nothing. And at Brewster's angle the reflected ray is perpendicular to the refracted ray.

The mnemonics, all six of them, in one place. Big n, slow and short. Red is receding. Order m, index n. Two-en-tee, mind the half. D for double and bright, a for aperture and dark. Half first, cosine-squared the rest.

And that is Wave Optics, end to end. Every formula you have met in this chapter is a consequence of one decision: treat light as a wave, and ask at every surface and every aperture where the wavefront goes next.
Chapter का आख़िरी section: quick-recall sheet। इसे exam की सुबह पढ़िए, और कुछ नहीं।

Map से शुरू कीजिए। ऊपर एक idea, wavefronts और Huygens का principle, और उससे लटकते चार नतीजे: Doppler, interference, diffraction, polarisation। आपने जो कुछ सीखा है वो इसी diagram पर कहीं न कहीं बैठा है।

Wavefront और Huygens। एक ही phase वाले points का locus, और ray उसके perpendicular। Point source spherical, line source cylindrical, दूर का source plane। हर point secondary source बनता है और wavelets का envelope नया front है। Refraction पर frequency बची रहती है; speed और wavelength नहीं।

Doppler। दूर जाना यानी redshift, यानी लंबी wavelength और कम frequency। पास आना यानी blueshift। सिर्फ़ radial component गिना जाता है, और जब भी wave किसी चलती चीज़ से टकराए या दो उल्टे किनारों की तुलना हो, दो का factor ढूँढिए।

Interference। Coherent यानी constant phase difference, इसलिए दो independent bulbs कोई fringes देते ही नहीं। Central fringe हमेशा bright। Fringe width एकसार और order से स्वतंत्र। Denser medium उसे छोटा करता है, और एक slit पर रखी glass sheet pattern को खिसकाती है पर spacing नहीं बदलती।

Thin film। Division of amplitude, और हर rarer-से-denser reflection पर half-wave loss। Reflected और transmitted conditions complementary हैं। बहुत पतली film reflection में काली दिखती है। Anti-reflection coating एक quarter-wave layer है, और Newton's rings का centre dark होता है और liquid में वो root n से सिकुड़ती हैं।

Diffraction। Apertures पर मुड़ना, जो तब दिखता है जब aperture wavelength जितना हो, और असल में ये एक wavefront का ख़ुद से interference है। Minima की condition double-slit की bright condition जैसी ही दिखती है और उल्टा मतलब रखती है। Central maximum दोगुना चौड़ा और कहीं ज़्यादा चमकीला। बड़ा aperture यानी बेहतर resolution।

Polarisation। सिर्फ़ transverse waves polarise होती हैं, इसीलिए light polarise हो सकती है और sound नहीं। पहले polaroid पर आधा, फिर हर अगले पर एक cosine squared। Crossed polaroids कुछ नहीं भेजते। और Brewster के angle पर reflected ray, refracted ray के perpendicular होती है।
छहों mnemonics, एक ही जगह। Big n, slow and short। Red is receding। Order m, index n। Two-en-tee, mind the half। D for double and bright, a for aperture and dark। Half first, cosine-squared the rest।
और यही है Wave Optics, शुरू से आख़िर तक। इस chapter में मिला हर formula एक ही फ़ैसले का नतीजा है: light को wave मानिए, और हर surface तथा हर aperture पर पूछिए कि wavefront आगे कहाँ जाता है।
